checks.Title: Seduce, don't just observe
checks.Evidence: There are strong sensory hooks that seduce before horror lands — Skillet Row's 'hot oil and wet concrete, and under that, something sweet,' Scraps ladling broth without breaking eye contact, the Glass sequence's tactile bloom — but much of the middle (job montages, clinic procedures, board mechanics) shifts into efficient exposition mode ('The subdermal work took three hours... six thread-anchors seated at the C6 vertebra') that explains world mechanics accurately without lingering on texture to make GLMZ feel irresistible first.
checks.Fix: Slow down the expository stretches (clinic installation, Ozzie's board economics, the Vane rate-splitting) to root each in one vivid sensory or emotional hook before the mechanical/informational payload, so allure consistently precedes or interlaces with the horror rather than horror riding alone on bare competent description.

checks.Title: Open with the world doing its work
checks.Evidence: The opening beats — Tavi and Reza leaving Ozzie's squat, the Gray Zone described through a character who 'hadn't stopped once' looking at the Thread, and the mundane texture of Skillet Row's booths and haggling — establish the world through routine, lived-in detail before any plot demand (the debtor job) arrives.

checks.Title: Gloss first mentions in-voice, never dump
checks.Evidence: Most terms land well in-voice ('civic neuretics everybody got seeded with,' 'the Thread... anchored somewhere near Crestwood, climbing until it stopped being visible'), but some proprietary nouns arrive with zero gloss and rely on context alone — 'CorpoNations' never appears at all, and terms like 'Axiom logistics,' 'Lotus-adjacent contract,' 'Helix-grade,' and 'Ashgrave perimeter' are dropped as pure brand-texture with no orienting cue for a first-time reader to anchor scale or stakes.
checks.Fix: Add a half-clause of sensory or functional context on first use of the corporate/geographic proper nouns (e.g., 'an Axiom logistics courier — one of the big orbital shippers' or a physical detail that signals Ashgrave's function) so newcomers can place them without breaking the in-voice flow.

checks.Title: Never an acronym before its term
checks.Evidence: Multiple acronyms appear with no expansion at all: 'Cermak Tier-2 consult' and 'the basic mesh', 'Helix-grade' haptic array, and most notably 'NSB'-style world jargon isn't used, but GLMZ-type acronyms like tech terms are absent of gloss — e.g., there are no acronyms like 'NSB' here, but the story does use unexplained shorthand terms without any acronym-expansion pattern at all (e.g., no acronyms are ever glossed in-voice before use, since none appear in strict acronym form, but comparable jargon like 'Tier-1 mesh,' 'Tier-2 consult,' and 'Helix-grade' are dropped as if pre-established).
checks.Fix: If any acronym is intended to appear in this story, introduce it once with a natural in-voice gloss of the full term (e.g., 'the Cermak Tier-2 neural consult' before shortening it), and audit all technical shorthand for the same treatment.

checks.Title: Give the POV character one human crack
checks.Evidence: The high-five callback across the whole node — 'the same crack as the squat, but bigger now, giddier' and later 'his hand came up an inch off his hip, old habit, reaching for a palm that wasn't there anymore' — gives Tavi a single tender, unguarded tell of attachment to Reza that he immediately buries by closing his hand around the pistol instead.

checks.Title: Land one beat past the handoff
checks.Evidence: The final beat—Tavi seeing Scraps hand a job to two fresh, wide-eyed nineteen-year-olds, his hand reaching for a palm that isn't there anymore, closing instead around the cold twin pistol, then simply 'He went to work'—resolves nothing plot-wise but adds the exact weight the rule calls for: the cycle restarting with new kids, the severed partnership, and the character hardening into the city's machinery.

checks.Title: Reward re-reading without requiring it
checks.Evidence: The recurring high-five motif works perfectly on a first read as a bonding gesture, but the final scenes deliberately track its erosion ('his hand didn't come up... they both watched it stay there') and the closing image ('his hand came up an inch off his hip, old habit, reaching for a palm that wasn't there anymore') recontextualizes every earlier slap as foreshadowing of the split — a detail that only fully lands once the reader knows the partnership ends.

checks.Title: Elevate, don't reconstruct
checks.Evidence: The prose reads as a self-contained, ground-up origin story (two nineteen-year-olds from a squat building a partnership) rather than a retrofit of continuity-laden material — worldbuilding terms like 'the Glass,' 'Substrate,' 'quanta,' and 'chrome' are introduced through action and context (e.g., 'The Glass didn't invent anything. It took what was already there and stripped away whatever usually kept a body from feeling all of it at once') rather than via expository seams that suggest a rewrite bolted onto existing lore.

checks.Title: Orient through GLMZ's five pillars
checks.Evidence: The story vividly renders neuretics (jack ports, mesh tiers, the Glass), nanites as ambient infrastructure (coverage percentages, healing warmth, gray zone thinning), and CorpoNations/gray zones as governing texture (Ashgrave perimeter, Vane's contracts, checkpoints), but AIs as agentic factional entities never appear at all, and the Schism is completely absent — there is no rift, no wound in reality, no physics-breaking event referenced anywhere in the text.
checks.Fix: Weave in at least one concrete reference to the Schism as a physical/historical rupture (e.g., a landmark, a no-go zone, or a character's offhand memory of it) and introduce or gesture at an AI faction with its own visible agenda operating in this world.
